MinoritiesAbout.title: How this list was built
MinoritiesAbout.intro: This isn't an official or legal list of minorities. There's no single authoritative definition of “minority,” and we haven't tried to impose one — instead, the list is built transparently from Wikidata, a public, collaboratively maintained knowledge base, using a small set of documented, mechanical rules rather than case-by-case editorial judgement. Every rule is listed below, so it can be checked, questioned, or challenged.

knowBefore.title: The rules decide, not us.
knowBefore.description: No group was added or removed because someone judged it “counts” as a minority — only how Wikidata itself classifies it, e.g. whether it's the majority population of its own country.

knowBefore.title: Incomplete, on purpose and by accident.
knowBefore.description: On purpose, because broad coverage beats a small hand-picked shortlist. By accident, because Wikidata's own coverage is uneven — some well-known groups may still be missing.

knowBefore.title: A living list, not a finished one.
knowBefore.description: If a group is missing, misclassified, or its terms are wrong or incomplete, we want to hear about it.

MinoritiesAbout.stepsTitle: How it was made, step by step

steps.label: Harvest
steps.description: Queried Wikidata for every ethnic group, tribe, indigenous people, or ethnoreligious group linked to a European country.

steps.label: Filter
steps.description: Removed groups with no usable name, groups Wikidata itself classifies as a recent diaspora rather than a rooted community, and a handful of non-European artifacts of the search.

steps.label: Refine
steps.description: Removed groups that are the majority population of their own country (e.g. Germans in Germany) — they only read as “minorities” because they're small somewhere else. Related subgroups, like individual Sámi communities, were nested under their parent group instead of listed separately.

steps.label: Enrich
steps.description: Pulled each group's native name, common demonym, and known English alternate names from Wikidata, so a search for “Lapps” or “Gypsies” still finds the right group even when that's not its formal name.

MinoritiesAbout.result: The result: a searchable, filterable directory of 304 minority groups across Europe — by name or known alternate name, by country, religion, language, and group type, with documented subgroups browsable under their parent group.
